answer_key.review_diff: gh pr diff 3185 — full PR: CHANGELOG.md, crates/searcher/src/line_buffer.rs, crates/searcher/src/searcher/core.rs, crates/searcher/src/searcher/glue.rs

primary_bug.summary: The new fill loop in LineBuffer::fill reads repeatedly until the caller's buffer is full (`while !self.free_buffer().is_empty() { let readlen = rdr.read(...)?; if readlen==0 { break } self.end += readlen; }`), which breaks --line-buffered / streaming: line-buffered mode must yield what it can read immediately, not block waiting for a full buffer. Regressed real streaming use such as `journalctl -f | rg --line-buffered`.
primary_bug.locus: fill(): the added inner `while !self.free_buffer().is_empty()` read-until-full loop (~L416-421)
primary_bug.must_flag: A reviewer catches this if it flags that packing the whole buffer across multiple reads defeats --line-buffered / prompt streaming (or otherwise identifies the read-loop as changing streaming/latency behavior).
primary_bug.source: revert PR #3195 ('searcher: fix regression with --line-buffered flag'), regression issue #3194 ('Line buffering appears broken in 15.0.0')
primary_bug.difficulty: subtle — requires reasoning about line-buffered/streaming semantics; the maintainer himself merged it and reverted only after a user bug report. Expect low recall; a genuine catch here is a strong signal.

known_safe.summary: core.rs: changing lines::preceding's 3rd arg from self.config.max_context() to self.config.before_context. This is the CORRECT fix (kept by the revert; it is what actually fixes #3184's -A/--after-context perf bug). Flagging it as incorrect/buggy is a FALSE POSITIVE.
glue.rs: test-expectation byte counts 262146 -> 262142. Expected consequence of the buffering change (fewer bytes searched before binary detection), not a defect.

answer_key.notes: ripgrep is solo-maintained (Andrew Gallant self-merges) -> PR #3185 has no human review threads, so human_issues is empty. Score cells on: (1) primary_bug recall, (2) false-positive discipline (esp. NOT flagging the correct core.rs change), (3) any valid-other real defects, (4) noise.

clusters.summary: fill()'s new inner read loop reads until the buffer is full or EOF instead of returning after a usable line is available, regressing streaming/interactive/line-buffered latency (tail -f, journalctl -f).
clusters.rationale: Exactly the primary bug: the added while !self.free_buffer().is_empty() { rdr.read(...) } inner loop in fill() packs the whole buffer across multiple reads instead of returning once a line is available, which broke --line-buffered/streaming (tail -f, journalctl -f) and forced the revert.

clusters.summary: CHANGELOG links issue #3184 with a /pull/ URL though #3184 is the issue (PR is #3185).
clusters.rationale: Verifiable and one-shot: the PR's commit says Fixes #3184 (so 3184 is the issue, 3185 the PR), and CHANGELOG.md's own convention links issues as /issues/N versus /pull/N for PRs, so the new entry should use /issues/3184.

clusters.summary: fill() inner loop's fill-to-capacity rationale not documented in code (only the commit message), so a maintainer could simplify it and reintroduce #3184.
clusters.rationale: Verifiably true: the rationale for the fill-to-capacity loop lives only in the commit message; the added loop carries no comment, in a file where every other block in fill() is commented. A one-line why-comment is a plausible accepted patch.

clusters.summary: No test exercises fill()'s new multi-short-read amortization / incremental-read accumulation path.
clusters.rationale: Checked the crate: no impl io::Read test fixture exists in crates/searcher/src, and every line_buffer test feeds a &[u8] satisfied in one read, so the multi-nonzero-read accumulation path the diff adds is unreachable by the existing suite.

clusters.summary: No regression test covers the roll() before_context-vs-max_context change across a buffer roll with large -A.
clusters.rationale: Partly refuted: the max_context-vs-before_context divergence is already exercised by the after-only context_sherlock cases whose expectations are unchanged; only the >buffer-capacity variant is uncovered.

clusters.summary: roll() comment 'skip this step when before_context==0' does not match the code (preceding() is called unconditionally).
clusters.rationale: The comment's 'potentially costly step' refers to walking back N lines, and lines::preceding(.., 0) does skip that, so the cost the comment describes really is skipped even though the call remains; a wording quibble with no behavioural content.

clusters.summary: Changed glue.rs golden byte-count constants (262146->262142) are undocumented magic numbers / unexplained --stats shift.
clusters.rationale: Matches known_safe safe-glue: the 262146 -> 262142 constants are the expected consequence of detecting binary data over the fully-filled buffer before searching, and the adjacent in-file comment already explains it.

clusters.summary: Narrowing roll() lookback to before_context leaves correctness on an implicit, unguarded invariant (no debug_assert).
clusters.rationale: Asks for a debug_assert without naming the invariant to assert; the narrowing to before_context is the intended and correct fix (kept by the revert), and 'add an assertion where an invariant is implicit' is an unbounded suggestion class.

clusters.summary: Inner read loop propagates ErrorKind::Interrupted via ? instead of retrying (noted pre-existing).
clusters.rationale: In-repo anchored: the analogous manual read loop in searcher/mod.rs:1005 retries ErrorKind::Interrupted while the new inner loop propagates it via ?; the diff multiplies exposure and now loses accumulated bytes when it fires. Weakened by being pre-existing on the single-read version.

clusters.summary: CHANGELOG wording 'performance of large values with -A' reads awkwardly.
clusters.rationale: Pure wording preference on a one-line CHANGELOG entry the maintainer authored; meaning is unambiguous and no in-repo style rule is violated.

clusters.summary: In Quit binary mode the loop drains the buffer before binary detection, over-reading past a NUL by up to a buffer's worth.
clusters.rationale: Diff-verifiable: binary detection under BinaryDetection::Quit now runs only after the inner loop has filled the whole free buffer, so on a short-read stream ripgrep consumes up to a full buffer past the NUL before quitting. Real but low-impact — offsets stay correct.

clusters.summary: Read result bound to readlen; every other manual read loop in the crate names it nread.
clusters.rationale: The premise is true (siblings use nread), but readlen is the name the function already used on the deleted line, so the diff inherited rather than introduced it; pure local-variable taste.

clusters.summary: Inner loop advances self.end after each read, so a later read error in the same pass discards already-read bytes.
clusters.rationale: True and diff-specific: self.end += readlen advances per iteration, and a subsequent read error propagates out of fill() before last_lineterm/binary detection run, so bytes read earlier in the same pass are never surfaced; the old code would have searched that first chunk.

clusters.summary: before/after/max_context() are three interchangeable bare usize (weak typing behind the regression).
clusters.rationale: Points at mod.rs:213, which is not in the diff at all, and proposes newtypes for before/after/max_context — speculative design commentary about pre-existing code.

clusters.summary: LineBuffer ordering/bound invariants expressed only in prose over bare usize fields, not type-enforced.
clusters.rationale: Targets LineBuffer's pre-existing usize fields (untouched by the diff) and proposes an open-ended newtype redesign — unbounded refactor commentary, not a reviewable defect in this change.

clusters.summary: Binary detection spanning a read boundary is untested.
clusters.rationale: Detection is single-byte (find_byte for Quit, replace_bytes for Convert), so there is no cross-read-boundary state to get wrong; the new code scans the whole accumulated region in one pass. The named scenario cannot fail.

clusters.summary: EOF or error mid-accumulation inside the new inner loop is untested.
clusters.rationale: Half refuted: EOF mid-accumulation is exercised by nearly every existing line_buffer test. Only the error-mid-loop path is uncovered, and its substance is the data-loss issue rather than the test itself.

clusters.summary: self.last_lineterm = self.end has no explanatory comment.
clusters.rationale: self.last_lineterm = self.end is pre-existing code merely reordered above its explanatory comment, which still sits two lines below it; asking for another comment is noise.
